review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the related definitions: refinementHistoryForcing_mem, rawRowAssignmentActionGraph_mem, and definable_structuralRefinementHistory. I read the other callers of structuralForcingCarrier_mem in GroundStructuralForcingHistoryConstruction.lean. Most other statements are tied to specific Fin-indexed GroundDefinableFunction interfaces, so I found no useful generalisation there. I only report the env-tuple form of the carrier membership lemma, which is a modest, API-level generalisation. I have not compiled the proposed statement.

findings.excerpt: theorem structuralForcingCarrier_mem (env : Fin 9 → ZFSet.{u}) (members : ∀ j, env j ∈ M.sets)
findings.problem: The lemma is stated only for an arbitrary 9-tuple `env : Fin 9 → ZFSet` with a blanket membership hypothesis `∀ j, env j ∈ M.sets`. The conclusion is about `structuralForcingCarrier (env 0) ... (env 8)`. This is more specialised than the mathematical content: the carrier of nine independent sets, each in `M.sets`. The sibling lemma `structuralAssignmentActionGraph_mem` in the same file takes the sets as implicit arguments with one membership hypothesis each. Because of the tuple form, every caller must build `![...]` and a nested `Fin.cases` proof of `∀ j, ...` just to apply it. The proof only uses `members 0`, `members 5` and `members 7` directly, and uses the other entries only through `fun j => members j.succ`.
findings.proposed_change:
State it with the sets as implicit arguments and one hypothesis each:
`theorem structuralForcingCarrier_mem {rows G nodes nodeOrder basis T T2 stages history : ZFSet.{u}} (hRows : rows ∈ M.sets) (hG : G ∈ M.sets) (hn : nodes ∈ M.sets) (hno : nodeOrder ∈ M.sets) (hb : basis ∈ M.sets) (hT : T ∈ M.sets) (hT2 : T2 ∈ M.sets) (hs : stages ∈ M.sets) (hh : history ∈ M.sets) (omega : ZFSet.omega ∈ M.sets) : M.structuralForcingCarrier rows G nodes nodeOrder basis T T2 stages history ∈ M.sets`.
Proof: `M.refinementHistoryForcing_mem pairing unions powers separation hRows hT hs ((M.definable_structuralRefinementHistory pairing unions powers separation collection).closed ![G,nodes,nodeOrder,basis,T,T2,stages,history] (Fin.cases hG (Fin.cases hn ...))) omega`, which is the same packing already done at the call site in `structuralForcingActionGraph_mem`. If the env form is still wanted, keep it as a one-line corollary, e.g. `structuralForcingCarrier_mem_env`, obtained from the new lemma by `members 0`, `members 1`, and so on. No degenerate case arises: the hypotheses are exactly those the old proof used, and `omega` is still required.
findings.benefit: All three call sites (here at line 177 and two in GroundStructuralForcingHistoryConstruction.lean) currently repack their already-available individual membership facts into a `Fin 9` tuple and a nested `Fin.cases` proof, only for the lemma to unpack them again. They could pass the hypotheses directly. The lemma would also match the style of `structuralAssignmentActionGraph_mem` and `refinementHistoryForcing_mem`.
